 Judgment

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 18.10.2022.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, SCCH - 25 3 MVC No. 159/2023 On 18.10.2022 at about 9.30 to 9.35pm when he was riding a Bajaj Discover vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA51ED5182 heading towards NH44 main Road SKF Company front service road, a Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA05MC6234 came on the same route from the opposite side with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and collided with the petitioner's vehicle.

As a result,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was taken to Mithra Hospital and thereafter shifted to St.John's Medical college hospital, admitted as an inpatient from 19.10.2022 to 01.12.2022, underwent surgeries and discharged with advice.
So far he has spent Rs.4,00,000/ towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,
At the time of accident he was hale and healthy, working as an Ironer at Nehal Trading and earning a sum of Rs.35,000/ per month.
Due to accidental injuries he lost his income.
He is put to great hardship and SCCH - 25 4 MVC No. 159/2023 mental agony and shock.
The accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA05MC6234.
The Hebbagodi Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.330/2022.
Therefore, the 1st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons the respondent No.1 did not appear hence placed exparte.
5. The objection of the respondent No.2.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of the Respondent No.1 in respect of the Innova Car bearing KA05 MC--6234.
Further contended that the accident was caused due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
The SCCH - 25 5 MVC No. 159/2023 petition is also bad for non compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134(c) of MV Act.
The driver of Innova Car did not have valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.

It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of Raja vs Thomas Kutty K.C on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172398822/
2 accident.
It contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, he sustained injuries on 18.10.2022 on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA05MC6234 by its driver as contended in the petition?
2. Whether Respondent No.2 proves that, the driver of the offended vehicle was driving the vehicle without holding valid and effective DL?
3. Whether the Petitioner he is entitled for Compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom?
4.
What order
or award?
The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.12.
Dr.Chidanand K.J.C got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.13 & 14.
He has also got examined Mr.Arulraj Y.  Medical Record Assistance and got marked Exs.P.15 to 19.
Mr.D.M.Sheelavanth - MRO at Mithra Multy Specialty Hospital as PW.4 and got marked Exs.P.20 to 24.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
9.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: In the Negative, Issue No.3: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 159/2023 REASONS 10.

Issue No.1: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA05MC6234, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.8.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination except the fact that the FIR was filed after 5 days of the accident, nothing worthwhile is elicited.

He has also got examined the MRO of St.John's Medical College and Hospital as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.15 to P.19 Authorization letter, police intimation, MLC register extract, OP record and IP record.
During his cross examination he has stated that he does not know if it is mentioned in Ex.P.17 MLC there is history of Alcohol dose.

He also has got examined another MRO at Mithra Multy Specialty Hospital Mr.D.M.Sheelavanth as PW.4 and got marked Exs.P.20 to 24 authorization letter, IP record, police intimation, MLC register extract and Xray with SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 159/2023 report 2 in Nos.
During his cross examination he has stated that the petitioner got discharged against the medical Raja vs Thomas Kutty K.C on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172398822/
3 advice on the same day of admission and he has taken only firstaid in their hospital.
The Respondent No.2 insurer has contended that there was sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
In order to prove their contention they have not examined any witness.
11. As per FIR, it was registered after 8 days of the accident on the complaint of the Wife of the petitioner.
Ex. P.2
spot mahazar and Ex.P.3 seizure mahazar are all in accordance with the statement given by the wife of the petitioner.
Ex. P.4
wound certificate shows that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries in an RTA dated 18.10.2022.
The IMV report also shows that the Innova vehicle has suffered damages.
To the notice given under Ex.P.6, the owner of the Innova vehicle has replied as per Ex.P.7.
The police have conducted investigation and filed the charge sheet as per Ex.P.8 against the driver of the Innova Car.
The respondent SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 159/2023 No.2 has contended that there is delay of 8 days in filing the FIR.
During the cross of PW.1 he has stated that his wife was taking care of him in the hospital and could not give the complaint on time.
All these documents show that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA05MC6234.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue Nos.2 & 3:
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.4.

As per Ex.P.4, the Petitioner has sustained (i) Laceration over right middle finger, (ii) Laceration over right finger, (iii) Two lacerations over right leg with deformity and (iv) tenderness over right hip.

Out of these injuries,
injury Nos.1 & 2 are simple and 3 & 4 are grievous in nature.
The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.13 & 14 clinical notes and Xray 2 in Nos.
He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed fracture right leg both bone distal 1/3rd fracture type 111a and right acetabulum fracture.
He further stated that the petitioner is suffering from disability of lower limb at 57% and to the whole body at 20%.
14. PW.2 in his cross examination has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
Except this nothing worthwhile is elicited.
Disability:
15. From the evidence of PW.2 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered three fractures i.e., fracture of both bones in the lower limb as well as acetabulam fracture.
So it will be difficult for him to sit and walk.
He has stated that he was working as a Ironer at Nehal SCCH - 25 11 MVC No. 159/2023 Trading.
This means that either he has to sit or stand for a long time.
This kind of disability will affect his day to day work.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 20%.

Monthly income:
Raja vs Thomas Kutty K.C on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172398822/
4 16.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as an Ironer at Nehal Trading and earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.15,500/ per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 35 years as could be made out from Ex.P.4/Wound Certificate as well as Affidavit.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.
The accident took place in the year 2022.
Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation: SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 159/2023 i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Mithra Hospital and at St.John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 19.10.2022 to 01.12.2022 and was diagnosed and underwent surgery which can be made out from Ex.P.9.
Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.4,00,000/ towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.10 for a sum of Rs.2,47,733/
There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.
SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 159/2023 iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries.

The petitioner has produced discharge summary of St.
John's Medical College Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.

Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,500/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
On perusal of Ex.P.4 as well as Affidavit, the petitioner's age is mentioned as 35 years.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 35 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 16.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.5,95,200/ (Rs.15,500/ x 12 x 16 x 20%=
Rs.5,95,200/) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
Raja vs Thomas Kutty K.C on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172398822/
5
The Petitioner was aged about 35 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained simple and grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 20% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs. 2,47,733/
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.15,500/ period

4. Loss of future income Rs.5,95,200/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/ happiness
6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.9,78,433/ If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.9,78,500/ and same is awarded under to the Petitioner.
Liability 18.
The Respondents have contended that the driver of the Innova Car did not have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
However, they have not proved their defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

However, as the policy existed as on the date of SCCH - 25 16 MVC No.
159/2023 accident
, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.25,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.9,78,500/ with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.

Accordingly, Issue No.2 is Raja vs Thomas Kutty K.C on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172398822/
6 held in the negative and Issue No.3 is held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.4: For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.9,78,500/ (Rupees Nine Lakhs Seventy Eight Thousand and Five Hundred only) along SCCH - 25 17 MVC No. 159/2023 with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.

On deposit of compensation and interest, 25% shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner for a period of 3 years in any N/S Bank and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules

. 
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
SCCH - 25 18 MVC No. 159/2023
Draw decree accordingly.
